candidate.answerReason: For the sorted positive lengths, compare the shortest-times-longest product with the middle-pair product. A gives 4 ≠ 6, B gives 18 ≠ 20, C gives 12 = 12, and D gives 16 ≠ 20. Only C can form a proportion.

methods.label: Compare extreme and middle products
methods.explanation: For proportional line segments, the product of the longest and shortest must equal the product of the other two: \(2\times6=12=3\times4\), so \(2:3=4:6\) holds. None of the other groups satisfies this condition.
methods.levelReason: Recognizing proportional segments by the cross-product property is within Grade 9 scope.

review.mathematicalCheck: For four positive lengths in increasing order, any equal-product pairing must pair shortest with longest against the middle pair.
